The position statements are divided by short standalone title-case lines that act as section headings: 'Core Position', 'Critical Issues', 'Recommended Solutions', 'Path Forward', 'Supporting Evidence', 'Impact of Current Requirements', 'Practical Solution', 'Legal Framework', 'Call to Action'. But every one of them is formatted exactly like body text: Normal style, no pPr, no bold, 12pt like all text, no extra spacing, not centered or numbered. The only visual cue is a short line without end punctuation followed by a paragraph. No paragraph uses a heading style or outline level ('heading 1'/'heading 2' are defined but unused).
notes.link_text: No hyperlinks.
notes.title: docProps/core.xml has no dc:title.
notes.other: HEADINGS DISPUTED (hardest call in batch): the lines plainly function as section headings of the position statements, and a reader would probably take them as headings from position and title case alone, but they have none of the visual heading cues (bold, size, caps, underline, numbering, spacing) the criterion lists. If 'acts as a heading' suffices it is a fail; if headings must look different from body text it is a pass. Publisher is an organisation of blind guide-dog users; text looks pasted from plain text/email.
